description: VX Drum Sequencer: a 16-step drum pattern sequencer with six voice lanes and an accent lane, sixteen pattern memories, and a polyphonic trigger output built to drive VX Drums

params.text: Chooses the memory that plays and that the grid edits; the lit button is the one playing, and while a cable is in MEM the buttons are locked and presses ignored
Cancels any hits waiting to fire and rewinds the pattern, so the next clock plays step 1, which is what a pulse at RST does
Writes a new beat into the memory playing now, each lane given a part that suits its instrument, a few ratchets sprinkled in and the memory's length kept

inputs.text: Advances the pattern one step per rising edge, reading high at 2V and needing a fall to 0.1V before the next edge counts; there is no clock inside, so feed it sixteenths
A rising edge cancels hits waiting to fire and rewinds the pattern, so the next clock plays step 1; a clock arriving on the same sample plays step 1 at once
Picks the memory, 0V for memory 1 up to 10V for memory 16 in steps of 0.625V; while a cable is here the memory buttons are locked and the lit one follows this voltage

outputs.text: Carries one voice per channel, 1 bass drum, 2 snare, 3 clap, 4 percussion, 5 closed hat, 6 open hat; every hit is a 10V pulse, 1ms long to start with, and a muted lane's channel stays silent
Carries a 10V pulse of the same length on every accented step, on the same sample as that step's hits and again with each ratchet repeat; an accented step with no hits pulses here too

notes: nothing plays until a clock pulse arrives at CLK, and unplugging the clock leaves the pattern where it stopped
click a pad in the grid to place or remove a hit, and drag across pads to paint them the way the first one went; the pads are one display widget, so none of them can be clicked for help
shift-click a lit voice pad to step its ratchet through x2, x3, x4 and back to a single hit, splitting the step into that many evenly spaced hits at the same strength
click a lamp in the row above the grid to set the memory's length; pads past the length keep their hits and draw dimmed, and each memory has its own length
click a lane label at the left of the grid to mute that lane; a muted lane neither sounds nor pulses at TRIG, and mutes are kept across a memory change
the AC lane at the bottom of the grid makes every voice on that step hit harder through the kit, and makes no sound of its own
two or more of these placed side by side and touching play one after another as one longer pattern; the leftmost takes the clock and reset, and every one of them carries the whole chain's hits
sound design belongs to VX Drums: a memory holds the seven lanes of hits with each hit's ratchet and chance, and its length, and nothing else
menu: Chain: head of N, or Chain: member M of N — shown only while this sequencer is part of a chain, and says which place in it this one holds; it changes nothing
Trigger length — the length of the pulses at TRIG and ACC: 1ms, 2ms, 5ms, 10ms, 20ms, 50ms, 100ms or 200ms, and every hit gets its own rising edge whichever is chosen
Randomize settings — ticks which of the seven lanes the RND button rewrites, with All and None at the bottom; an unticked lane keeps every hit it has
Chance mode — draws every lit pad as a bar whose height is its chance and lets you drag a pad up or down to set it, the top of the pad being 100% and the bottom 0%
Export pattern… — writes the memory playing now to a JSON file
Import pattern… — replaces the memory playing now with one read from a JSON file
Clear pattern — empties the memory playing now and puts its length back to 16
Ratchet ×2, Ratchet ×3, Ratchet ×4, Single, in a lit voice pad's own right-click menu — splits that step into that many evenly spaced hits, or returns it to one
Chance, in a lit pad's own right-click menu — the odds that the pad plays each time its step comes round: 100%, 75%, 50%, 25%, 10% or 0%
Copy, Paste, Clear, in a memory button's own right-click menu — puts that memory on the system clipboard, writes the clipboard into it, or empties it and sets its length back to 16

inputs.0: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.2:
0 to 10V · stepped · one channel only

a negative voltage does nothing here.
